A Portuguese navigator who led the first voyage from Europe to India by sea, around Africa, in 1497 to 1499.

He left Lisbon in July 1497 with four ships. Following Bartolomeu Dias, who had rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488, he swung far out into the South Atlantic, then sailed up the east African coast to the Swahili towns of Mombasa and Malindi. At Malindi he took on a pilot who guided him across the Indian Ocean, and in May 1498 he reached Calicut, centre of the pepper trade. Its ruler, the Zamorin, was unimpressed by his gifts. Many of his men died on the voyage, most of scurvy, but the spices he brought back paid for it many times over.

He went back in 1502 with a war fleet and used brutal force against Calicut and Muslim shipping. He died at Cochin in 1524 as viceroy of India. His route gave Portugal an empire of trading forts, from Goa to Malacca, and broke into the Indian Ocean trade.
sum: A Portuguese navigator who led the first voyage from Europe to India by sea, around Africa, in 1497 to 1499.
